rationale.usefulness: Concrete multimodal inputs, text output, documented endpoints and low lower-tier rates make repeated extraction, classification and media logging practical experiments. The report accurately exposes the full-request premium above 200K tokens, reasoning-token accounting, application-owned tool execution and per-item review requirements. These details support useful trials while avoiding an untested cost-saving promise.
rationale.impact: An inexpensive execution model with broad input modalities and published integration contracts could materially expand the repeated work affordable inside agent systems. Meta's presented efficiency and workflow results support significant potential, but mixed harnesses, vendor reporting and the unavailable evaluation report do not justify exceptional field-wide significance.
rationale.novelty: The specific multimodal worker profile, long output capacity and documented price/performance position offer meaningful differentiation. The planner/worker pattern and hosted endpoint design are established approaches, and the independent SVG observation is too narrow to substantiate a qualitatively new capability.
rationale.maturity: A named production model, account/key setup, multiple API formats, price tiers and team rate limits make access concrete. Reliability, endpoint combinations, structured-output failure behavior, latency and workload-level costs were not exercised. The conflicting photo-example totals and mixed benchmark conditions are properly disclosed and limit stronger readiness claims.
rationale.openness: Public documentation and familiar endpoint formats offer useful integration portability, but no downloadable checkpoint, weight license or training reproducibility was established. Hosted access and an unresolved full service-terms review keep openness low; API Standard-mode training treatment is correctly separated from Muse Code Contributor settings and from retention.
